results.title: Kingsoft Cloud Hikes GPU and Storage Tariffs as AI Computing Demand Surges| TMTPOST
highlights: TMTPOST — Cloud infrastructure provider Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited has instituted sweeping price increases across its artificial intelligence computing and data storage product portfolios, according to updated tariff disclosures published on its official website. The hardware rate adjustments scale across two primary enterprise categories to offset rising global infrastructure and power overheads. Service fees for high-performance AI computing nodes and related graphics processing workloads will rise between 15% and 50%. Concurrently, subscription tariffs for scale-out file storage products and data management services will see an upward adjustment ranging from 30% to 50%. The structural pricing overhaul arrives as enterprise infrastructure vendors navigate intense global supply constraints for specialized accelerator chips and high-bandwidth memory modules. Industry analysts note that the rate hike mirrors a broader strategic pivot among domestic cloud platforms to pass escalating hardware procurement and operational energy costs directly to downstream developer clients amid the generative AI training boom.

results.title: Hetzner raises cloud prices for new orders; CPX and CCX more than double
highlights:
Since June 15, 2026, new Hetzner Cloud servers cost more. In Germany and Finland, CX23 went from $4.99 to $6.49/mo and CPX22 from $9.49 to $22.99/mo, before IPv4 and VAT.

By Saurabh Khatri · Published Oct 18, 2026

Hetzner raised the prices of its cloud servers on June 15, 2026, at 8 AM CEST. The new prices apply to new orders and to rescales of existing cloud servers. Hetzner’s price adjustment page lists the old and new price of every cloud plan in Germany, Finland, the US and Singapore, plus new prices for its dedicated servers.

...

The CX and CAX lines rose by roughly a quarter to a third. The CPX and CCX lines rose far more: most of their plans more than doubled.

Germany (Falkenstein, Nuremberg) and Finland (Helsinki), USD per month, excluding IPv4 and VAT:

| Plan | Before | From June 15, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CX23 | $4.99 | $6.49 |
| CX33 | $7.99 | $9.99 |
| CX43 | $13.99 | $18.49 |
| CAX11 | $5.49 | $6.99 |
| CAX21 | $9.49 | $12.49 |
| CPX22 | $9.49 | $22.99 |
| CPX32 | $15.99 | $41.99 |
| CCX13 | $18.49 | $50.49 |
| CCX23 | $36.99 | $101.49 |

For the US locations (Ashburn and Hillsboro), the page lists CPX and CCX plans, and the CPX plans roughly tripled. CPX11 went from $6.99 to $20.49 a month, CPX21 from $13.99 to $37.49 and CPX31 from $24.99 to $73.49. CCX13 in the US went from $19.99 to $50.99. In Singapore, CPX12 went from $9.49 to $17.99 and CCX13 from $32.49 to $63.49.

## Who pays the new prices

- New cloud servers ordered from June 15, 2026.
- Existing cloud servers that you rescale.
- Orders placed before June 15 but delivered after it keep the old prices.

Hetzner’s page also warns that certain changes to servers with legacy pricing may move them to the current prices, and links to an FAQ that lists those actions. The page gives no reason for the increase. All prices on it exclude VAT and the IPv4 address, which is billed separately.

Dedicated servers got new prices on the same date, but the page lists only the new ones, so the size of that change can’t be read from it.

results.title: H100 SXM Down 9.4% in GPU Rental Market — Week of June 8 - June 14, 2026 | AIMC | AIMC
highlights:
H100 SXM average hourly rental rates fell 9.4% week-over-week, from $3.06 to $2.77, the largest single-SKU percentage decline across the 30 marketplaces AIMC tracked during the June 8–14 reporting window. The move was not isolated: nine of the ten most-active SKUs by observation volume posted negative week-over-week changes, with the A40 (-7.1%, $0.75 to $0.70), L40S (-6.8%, $1.71 to $1.59), and A100 SXM 80GB (-6.2%, $1.88 to $1.76) all registering declines of meaningful magnitude. The RTX 3090 was the lone gainer among the top movers, adding 4.8% to reach $0.36/hour. Across 7,822 total observations and 106 distinct SKUs, the breadth of softness warrants examination by segment — high-end data center GPUs, professional mid-tier cards, and consumer-class hardware each behaved differently, and the analysis that follows addresses each in turn.

...

## Headline Movements

| GPU | Last Week Avg | This Week Avg | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.06 | $2.77 | -9.4% |
| A40 | $0.75 | $0.70 | -7.1% |
| L40S | $1.71 | $1.59 | -6.8% |
| A100 SXM 80GB | $1.88 | $1.76 | -6.2% |
| RTX 3090 | $0.34 | $0.36 | +4.8% |

...

This week's data spans 30 marketplaces with 7,822 total listing observations across 106 distinct GPU SKUs.

H100 pricing ranged from $1.00/hour at ionet to $5.49/hour at togetherai across 20 marketplaces.

B200 pricing ranged from $3.50/hour at hyperstack to $9.95/hour at togetherai across 9 marketplaces.

L40S pricing ranged from $0.48/hour at tensordock to $2.48/hour at qubrid across 13 marketplaces.

A100 pricing ranged from $0.78/hour at synpixcloud to $4.19/hour at ovhcloud across 16 marketplaces.

...

The most striking pattern in this week's data is the broad-based softening across high-end data center GPUs, with training-class silicon bearing the sharpest declines. AIMC's data shows the H100 SXM falling 9.4% week-over-week from $3.06 to $2.77, the A40 dropping 7.1% to $0.70, and the L40S declining 6.8% to $1.59 — all moving in the same direction and within the same reporting window of June 8–14, 2026. When SKUs spanning different use cases and price tiers move together like this, it suggests a demand-side rather than a supply-side driver, since supply constraints tend to affect individual SKUs or families rather than the broader market simultaneously. The notable outlier is the RTX 3090, which moved in the opposite direction, gaining 4.8% to $0.36 — a divergence that, while small in absolute terms, stands out precisely because of how uniform the downward pressure was elsewhere.

...

This weekly report is generated from pricing data collected daily across all authorized data partners listed at aiminingco.com/data-partners. Coverage includes on-demand rates published by each marketplace. Spot pricing, reserved instance rates, and enterprise contracts are excluded.

results.title: Hetzner-Preiserhöhung Juni 2026: CPX und CCX bis +176% - unsere Einordnung
highlights:
Hetzner war für viele - auch für uns - jahrelang die naheliegende Antwort auf teure Hyperscaler: günstig, solide, in der EU betrieben. Genau deshalb müssen wir die jüngste Preisrunde klar benennen. Zum 15. Juni 2026 hebt Hetzner die Cloud-Preise erneut an, und bei den dedizierten-vCPU-Linien CPX und CCX geht es um bis zu rund 176% nach oben. Das ist keine Feinjustierung mehr, das verschiebt die Rechnung.

...

Es ist bereits die zweite Preisrunde 2026. Schon zum 1. April gab es eine breitere Anpassung von bis zu rund 37%, die auch Bestandskunden traf. Die Runde zum 15. Juni trifft nun gezielt die leistungsstärkeren Cloud-Linien - und sie gilt laut Hetzner nur für Neubestellungen und Rescales; bestehende Server behalten ihre Konditionen.

Die Größenordnung (Deutschland/Finnland, EUR/Monat) laut Hetzners eigener Preisanpassungs-Doku:

| Plan | alt | neu | Änderung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CX23 (Cost-Optimized) | 3,99 € | 5,49 € | +37,6% |
| CAX11 (Cost-Optimized, ARM) | 4,49 € | 5,99 € | +33,4% |
| CPX22 (dediziert vCPU) | 7,99 € | 19,49 € | +143,8% |
| CPX52 | 36,49 € | 100,49 € | +175,3% |
| CCX13 (dediziert) | 15,99 € | 42,99 € | +168,9% |
| CCX63 | 374,49 € | 853,49 € | +127,9% |

Kurz: Die günstigen Cost-Optimized-Linien (CX/CAX) steigen moderat (rund 33-38%). Die dedizierten-vCPU-Linien CPX (rund +144-176%) und CCX (rund +113-169%) ziehen drastisch an.

...

Parallel ordnet Hetzner das Dedicated-Portfolio neu: Alle Modelle bekommen die Zusätze -1/-2/-3, dazu eine neue „-1-Ltd"-Linie (Limited, begrenzte Stückzahl aus günstiger beschaffter Hardware, zu attraktiven Konditionen). Die einmaligen Setup-Gebühren sinken deutlich für die meisten Dedicated-Server - dafür wird dieser Posten in eine höhere Monatsrate eingerechnet. Für Neubestellungen werden dedizierte Server damit teurer, aber moderater als die Cloud-CPX/CCX; Branchenberichte sprechen von überschaubaren Aufschlägen, bei einzelnen Serien rund einem Fünftel. Bestehende Dedicated-Verträge behalten ihre Konditionen; die Änderung greift nur bei Neubestellungen.

results.title: Spot vs On-Demand vs Reserved Cloud GPUs: Comparison 2026
highlights:
Spot Instances let you purchase spare, unused GPU capacity at a deep discount. The trade-off is real: the provider reclaims the hardware on short notice when demand picks up. AWS gives you 2 minutes. Google Cloud gives 30 seconds. Spot works well when your workload tolerates a restart.

On-Demand is the standard hourly option. No contract, no commitment, no interruption risk. You start the GPU when you need it and stop when you’re done. Billing stays predictable; the rate stays high.

Reserved or Committed Use requires that you enter into a 1- or 3-year contract. The provider, in turn, reduces your hourly charge. The savings are real and significant for workloads that are always on and stable.

...

Here’s a number people don’t always believe: AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure all offer Spot GPU instances at 60% to 91% off On-Demand pricing. Google Cloud’s Spot discounts for GPU instances reach as high as 91%. That’s not a typo.

2026 pricing snapshot (approximate AWS On-Demand vs Spot rates):

| GPU Model | On-Demand/hr | Spot/hr | Savings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA T4 | ~$0.53 | ~$0.16 – $0.22 | Up to 70% |
| NVIDIA A100 40GB | ~$3.20 | ~$0.90 – $1.30 | Up to 72% |
| NVIDIA H100 80GB | ~$3.90 | ~$1.95 – $2.50 | Up to 60% |

Those numbers compound fast. A team running A100s for 720 hours a month On-Demand pays roughly $2,304. On Spot, the same team might pay $936. Over twelve months, the difference is over $16,500 per single GPU. For teams running multiple GPUs, the savings become transformational.

...

The real value here is simplicity. You don’t commit to anything. You don’t need fault-tolerance logic in your job scheduler. You start the GPU, do your work, stop. It’s a great thing not having to think about it when you are creating cycles, experimenting, doing a quick demonstration for your client or even working on one-off projects. 

2026 On-Demand pricing (guestimate hourly pricing per provider):

| GPU Model | AWS | Google Cloud | Azure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA T4 | ~$0.53/hr | ~$0.35/hr | ~$0.40/hr |
| NVIDIA A100 40GB | ~$3.20/hr | ~$3.00/hr | ~$3.40/hr |
| NVIDIA H100 80GB | ~$3.90/hr | ~$3.00/hr | ~$6.98/hr |

Azure H100 at nearly $7/hour versus Google Cloud at $3.00 is a good reminder: On-Demand rates vary dramatically across providers, and provider choice matters as much as pricing model choice.

...

Reserved pricing is simple in principle: commit to using a GPU for one or three years, and the provider cuts your rate significantly. On AWS, a 1-year commitment saves around 40% versus On-Demand. Up to 71% will be saved through a 3-year commitment.

On-Demand (2026 approx) vs AWS A100 Reserved:

| Option | Hourly Rate | Monthly Cost | Savings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| On-Demand | ~$3.20 | ~$2,304 | Baseline |
| 1-Year Reserved | ~$1.90 | ~$1,368 | ~40% |
| 3-Year Reserved | ~$0.92 | ~$662 | ~71% |

On a 3-year Reserved plan, you’re paying $662/month for a GPU costing $2,304/month On-Demand. For teams that have consistent, predictable loads, the math doesn’t work out in favor of them.

results.title: GPU rental prices look like a leading indicator for Dell and Arm stock | Ornn News
highlights:
The Ornn H100 rental price index moves Dell and Arm three weeks before the stocks move, a forward signal that holds at the 1 percent significance level. The same index has no predictive grip on Nvidia, the company that makes the chips. 1

...

- The Ornn H100 price index leads Dell (DELL) and Arm (ARM) by three weeks at +0.51 forward correlation to each. Rising GPU prices time the entry on those names, not Nvidia.
- Nvidia shows no forward relationship at -0.05 (p of 0.64), trading coincident with the rental market rather than lagging it. Only Dell and Arm clear both the correlation and Granger bar across the 16-name AI universe.
- The H100 index spiked roughly 64 percent in three weeks from late April and sits near 2.59 dollars per GPU-hour now. That tightening has historically front-run Dell and Arm upside by about three weeks.

...

GPU rental prices are the cleanest real-time read on AI compute demand that exists. When H100 capacity tightens, the rental price rises within days, well before any company reports a quarter. The Ornn H100 SXM index is that price, updated daily, with two years of history behind it.

The index is not a smooth ramp. It fell almost continuously from roughly 3.15 dollars per GPU-hour in mid-2024 to a 1.63-dollar trough in early February 2026 as supply caught up with demand.

Then it snapped. From about 1.98 dollars on April 30 it spiked to a 3.24-dollar peak on May 19, a 64 percent move in three weeks and 98 percent off the February trough. It has since eased to 2.59 dollars. 1 

That spike is a demand signal. The question for capital is simple. Does the rental price move before the stocks that sell into the same demand, and if so, which ones.

...

### A hold above 2.70 dollars extends the tightening

A sustained hold above 2.70 dollars per GPU-hour would extend the tightening that has front-run Dell and Arm upside. A break back below 2.20 dollars would flip the three-week signal negative.
